findings.problem: The bar exists, is a live region, names Ctrl Z and is silent at rest — all of which the gate proves — but it is never on screen at the moment it has something to say. Driven at all five widths: press +7 with the editor open and the bar's viewport top measures 1252px in an 844px phone, 1319 in 1024, 1257 in 900, 1258 in a 1280x900 window and 1288 in 1440x960. inViewport is false every time, because it sits at the foot of the field below roughly 1400px of measure. Worse at the two widths where the editor is a sheet: scrolled all the way to the bottom at 390 and 768 the bar is physically underneath the fixed .b-edit — elementFromPoint over it returns .b-stepRead — so while the editor is open the Undo control cannot be reached by pointer at any scroll position. The owner sees the row move and the count change; the offer to take it back is announced to a screen reader and shown to nobody. That is the round-1 remediation delivered half-way: the gesture works, the promise around it does not.
findings.fix: Keep exactly one .b-undo node and move it to where the change is being made. In openEditor(), after building the editor node, appendChild the existing root.querySelector('.b-undo') as the last child of .b-edit (appendChild moves, so there is still one instance, one role="status" and one Ctrl Z legend, and the gate's 'there is exactly one of it' still holds). In closeEditor(), move the same node back to the field, inserted before .b-foot, so a change made and then closed still shows its way back. paintUndo already resolves the bar with root.querySelector, so it needs no change. Add margin-top:4px and border-top:1px solid var(--fore-16) to .b-undo when it is inside .b-edit so it reads as the panel's foot rather than a fifth field. Then add the assertion that is missing: after one stepper press, at every viewport in the config, assert the bar's rect is inside the viewport and that document.elementFromPoint at its centre is inside the bar.

findings.problem: Driven: the item count goes 7 to 6, the row is gone, nothing is pushed to history, the undo bar stays data-empty="true" and display:none, and Ctrl+Z afterwards restores nothing — the count stays 6. Focus lands on body. So the surface's one destructive action is the only action outside the reversibility system that already guards a one-day move, and it takes the keyboard user's place with it. It also sits one tab stop from "Done", at the same 35px height, the same border, the same adjacency, with no confirmation and no second step. A wedding planner deleting the wrong line has no path back and no sentence telling them what just left the plan.
findings.fix: In the delete branch of wireOwner, before item.remove(), push {kind:"delete", id, title, away, visibility, node:item, index} onto history and call paintUndo(root). Teach paintUndo a second sentence keyed on kind: 'Last change: ' + title + ' removed.' Teach undo() to handle kind==="delete" by re-appending the stored node to the measure, calling place(measureEl) and focusing its .b-grab. Move focus deterministically at delete time rather than letting it fall to body: focus the .b-grab of the next nearest remaining item, or the "Add a moment" button when the list is empty. Add assertions that delete is undoable by button and by Ctrl+Z, that the bar names the removal, and that document.activeElement is never document.body after a delete.

findings.problem: Measured at 390, 768, 1024, 1280 and 1440. Opening a row's editor — by mouse or by Enter — never moves focus into it, and the panel renders before the rows in DOM order, so from the row you just opened, forward Tab walks away into the next rows and the editor is behind you: from row 4 at 1440 it takes eight Shift+Tabs, past every earlier row's control, to reach the first stepper. The grab carries no aria-expanded and no aria-controls, and the panel has no role, no name and no heading, so nothing announces that a panel opened or which moment it edits. At 768 the fixed sheet completely buries the "Menu tasting at The Orchard" row and its own .b-grab — elementFromPoint over that control returns .b-edit — which is an occluded but still-tabbable control, the one variant of the invisible-focusable class the gate's opacity and display test cannot see.
findings.fix: Give .b-edit id="b-edit", role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at a new h3 inside it that names the moment being edited; give .b-grab aria-controls="b-edit" and aria-expanded that flips in openEditor/closeEditor. In openEditor, after place(), call the -7 stepper's focus() and scrollIntoView({block:"nearest"}) on the edited row, so the next Tab is inside the panel and the row you are moving stays visible. Below 1280, where .b-edit is position:fixed, add padding-bottom to .b-field equal to the sheet's measured offsetHeight + 24 while data-editor-open is set, so the sheet has a reserved band and no row or .b-grab can sit under it. Assert: after opening, document.activeElement is inside .b-edit; after opening at every viewport, no .b-grab centre resolves through elementFromPoint to .b-edit.

findings.problem: Driven: pressing "Add a moment" leaves the item count at 7. It opens the editor on the first existing moment with that moment's title pre-filled and "Delete this moment" sitting under it, and focus does not move, so a keyboard user gets no signal that anything happened at all. Second: the title field discards what you type. Filling #b-edit-title with 'Send the invitations to everyone' and pressing Done leaves the row reading 'Send the invitations' — no warning, no history entry, nothing said. On a surface whose entire subject is one person's own words, the single field that holds those words is the one control that throws them away, and this direction's own stated rule is that anything not built has no button element.
findings.fix: For the title: bind an input listener on #b-edit-title that writes the value to the row's .b-title through setAttribute('data-full', value) then C.settle() so the word-safe clamp stays idempotent, refreshes the .b-grab aria-label via grabLabel, and on blur or Done pushes {kind:"title", id, from, to} to history with the sentence 'Last change: renamed to ' + to + '.' For add: either build it — append a new .b-item with data-away set to the nearest day not already occupied, an empty title, open its editor with focus in #b-edit-title, push {kind:"add"} to history — or apply the direction's own rule and replace the button with inert("Adding a moment is not built yet"), which is a one-line change. Do not leave a button whose label promises a verb the file does not have. Assert both: typed title survives Done, and pressing add either increases .b-item count or is not a button.

findings.problem: There is no data-visibility rule anywhere in b.css — grep returns nothing. Toggling to Hidden changes the attribute, the 11px uppercase mono chip from SHOWN to HIDDEN, and the accessible name; measured, the row's opacity stays 1 and its title colour stays rgb(255,255,255). A moment the couple's families will never see is drawn exactly as heavy as one they will, and the only difference on a 1400px measure is one word at 62% ink in the smallest type on the page. The gate's assertion is named 'the row follows the toggle in ink and in words' but reads only the attribute, the chip word and the label, so the ink half of its own claim is unenforced. The toggle is also not pushed to history: guest visibility, the highest-stakes decision an owner makes on this screen, has no undo while moving a date one day does.
findings.fix: Add to b.css: .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-title { color: var(--fore-46); font-weight: 400; } .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-away, .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-date { color: var(--fore-46); } .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] .b-tick { background: transparent; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--fore-28); } so a hidden moment reads as an outline on the rail against a filled one, in ink density only. In the visButton click handler, push {kind:"visibility", id, title, from, to} to history and paintUndo, with 'Last change: ' + title + ' hidden from guests.' / ' shown to guests.' Extend the gate assertion to compare the computed colour of .b-title before and after the toggle and require it to differ.

biggestWin: The primary gesture. setAway is genuinely the only writer of an item's position and every fact — the count, the date line, the accessible name, the readout, the gap note, the lead marker — is derived from the one date it produces, so nothing drifts; the readout sits on its own line at a fixed measure, so no button moves out from under the cursor; the page keeps its scroll and its focus through every press; the ceiling states itself in a sentence instead of swallowing the press; Escape and Done both hand focus back to the row that opened the editor. Under the hand, changing a date on this surface now feels like Linear, and round 1's dominant defect is properly gone — that alone is worth more than a point. What stands between this and 9.5 is not a different decision and it is not polish: it is roughly a day of build in one file. Four of the five findings above are small, bounded edits to render-b.js — put the undo bar inside the editor, put delete and visibility and the title into the same history stack, move focus into the panel you just opened, and either build the add button or turn it into inert text — plus five lines of CSS to make a hidden moment look hidden. Nothing here needs the architecture reopened; the direction is right and the last fifteen per cent of its behaviour has not been written yet.
